newsitem.title: UK: BA threatens to ax domestic routes - paper.
newsitem.headline: BA threatens to ax domestic routes - paper.

text.p: British Airways Plc is threatening to cut domestic routes to Belfast, Newcastle and Plymouth if it is forced to surrender takeoff slots at London's Heathrow as a condition of its planned alliance with American Airlines, said the Observer newspaper on Sunday.
The report said that BA has put the regional services on the block as talks with competition authorities and the Government enter the final stage.

Washington has made any approval of the BA/American alliance conditional on getting open skies with Britain, and in particular in getting open access for all U.S. carriers to Heathrow, Europe's most popular airport.

But rival U.S. and British carriers say Heathrow is so overcrowded that open access would be meaningless unless they were to be granted some of British Airways' 38 percent share of existing takeoff and landing slots.
